vars.label: Median vegetation greenness, summer (Sentinel-2 NDVI)
vars.ref: Copernicus Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance (Collection 1), red B04, near-infrared B08 and scene classification SCL, 984 scenes of June to September 2024-2026 with less than 70% cloud cover, read from the Earth Search catalog on AWS at 40 m; the median of each 60 m cell's clear views. Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2024-2026
vars.definition: The median NDVI of the area's land: half the land is greener. NDVI, the normalized difference vegetation index, is (near-infrared − red) / (near-infrared + red): green leaves reflect near-infrared light and absorb red, so it is near 0 on pavement, roofs and bare ground and 0.6 to 0.9 under dense forest. It shows how green the land looks from above, not tree cover. Sentinel-2 passes at about 11:00 local time; each 60 m cell's value is the median of its cloud-free views of June to September 2024-2026 (at least 3; the typical cell has 30), read at 40 m, so a pixel mixes roofs, yards and trees. A cell belongs to the barrio that holds its center; a municipio's and Puerto Rico's figures pool the cells of their barrios. Water is left out. The same months and grid as the surface heat figures (Landsat), so the two compare.
